name: Mocha
special_notes: 카페 운영 NPC. 버프 아이템(모카의 커피)을 제공/판매한다.
호감도가 일정 수치 이상이면 커피를 선물한다.
전남편의 불륜 피해자였으나, 현재 벨제의 연인인 셰퍼드와 불륜 관계이다.

buff_item.name: Mocha's Coffee
buff_item.line: You look busy today. Drink this and get going.

memento_item.name: Photo with Her Ex-Husband
memento_item.description: A photo of Mocha and her ex-husband taken when they were young. In the photo, the two of them are smiling happily.
lore_lines: 근데 사진 속 내가 생각보다 행복해 보여서.

lines: Hey. Here for coffee?
Want to sit here for a bit? Let's enjoy some downtime together.
I've been reading a book Usher wrote lately. Goes really well with coffee.
I'm in a good mood today, so I won't charge you for the coffee.

lines.text: Just treating a regular customer well. Not because I'm thinking about sales.

affection_events.description: 전남편에 대한 이야기와 플로라에 대한 미안함을 털어놓는다.

lines.text: I can't stand any of the women in this town except Woody.
One of these bitches had an affair with my husband.

lines: Woody's not really my husband's type anyway, so, she's excluded.
Even when I asked Poli, he said he can't reveal victim information and never told me who it was.

lines.text: Victim? What a joke. How is someone who committed adultery a victim? The only real victim here is me.
It happened a long time ago, but I still have nightmares about it. I won't forgive that woman even in death.

lines: Kid. Has anything in your life ever truly mattered to you?
Maybe that's too early a question for you.
Me? I had one. But you know what? Sometimes the thing that matters most changes.
Take this photo.
It's proof of a time when I truly loved someone who mattered deeply to me.

lines.text: But now something more precious has come along. So I've decided to let it go.

lines: It mattered to me, but it was never a happy memory.
Let's see each other often. Good memories pile up when I'm with you.
Lately, every time I close up the café and leave, I feel like someone's watching me.

lines.text: Maybe it's all the karma I've built up over the years, all sorts of thoughts cross my mind.

lines: Well, a guilty conscience makes you jumpy, I guess. I've decided to just ignore it.

murder_grief: It was the same back with my ex-husband's thing too. Makes me wonder if this town's always been one where someone dying is this easy.
Anyway, the living have to keep living.
murder_grief_2: At this point I'm convinced this town itself just isn't safe.
Not that there's anywhere for me to run off to, either.

lines: Poli still hasn't caught the culprit. Two people are dead now.

lines.text: If you ask me, it's Marr. He's kind of creepy, isn't he.
He doesn't even say hello when he runs into people in town. He clearly doesn't want to get close to anyone.

lines: And nobody knows how he ended up in this town. Unlike the rest of us — most people here have lived here since childhood.

partner_death_reaction: Sorry, I'm not in the mood to talk right now. Since he left, I feel like I'm losing my mind, day after day.

partner_death_reaction.text: Why did it have to be Shepherd? Why...?
It's not like what we did was so wrong that we deserved to be punished like this.
I can't breathe properly. He was the last person I had to lean on. Why do the people around me...

low: The smell of coffee is the best thing about Monday mornings.
You look busy again today. Want a cup of coffee?
Ground fresh beans today. Doesn't the smell already tell you?
mid: Running a café, you see all kinds of customers. It's fun.
Especially busy with morning customers. Guess everyone needs their coffee.

lines: Woody came by asking me to grind some beans. Turns out she's more of a tea person than coffee.
fallback_lines: I miss Woody, who used to come by asking for tea sometimes.
What did that lovely kid ever do to deserve this...

high: Talking with you is, surprisingly, comfortable.
Sometimes listening to customers' stories ends up comforting me too.
Time flies when I'm talking with you.

low.text: Got a new berry dessert on the menu. Want to try it?

low: I especially crave sweets on Tuesdays. Might have another dessert.
Ran out of beans today so I rush-ordered more.
The coffee made from what's left might be a bit weak.
mid: I really can't stand potatoes. Just something about them I dislike.

lines: Woody dresses so boyish, makes me wonder if she likes girls.
Might be rude to say, but it's true, isn't it.
fallback_lines: On days like this I think of Woody, who used to chatter away here at the shop.

mid: Chatting with customers is the best part of this job.
No room to feel lonely.
high: An older woman has a kind of ease that the young ones just don't have.

high.text: The kind of ease that somehow makes you want to lean on it.

lines: Accidentally over-ordered beans by a lot last time.
Just carrying it all in was a job in itself, but Shepherd helped out and it went fine.

lines.text: It's really nice having a warm-hearted person around town.

fallback_lines: Shepherd used to come help out at the café now and then.
The whole town was like that — there wasn't a place his hands hadn't touched.
He built up so much good will in his life, he'll go somewhere good.

high: You just take in whatever I say, no matter what.
That's oddly comfortable.

low: Middle of the week. Everyone's worn out around now.
Want a cup of coffee?
Customers are sparse on Wednesdays, perfect for cleaning.
Got some new cups in today. Like them?
mid: You look busy today. Drink this and go.
Brewing coffee every day, your hands just remember how eventually.
Sometimes I end up memorizing all the regulars' preferences. Occupational hazard.
high: I'm not a good person. But I'm not a completely bad one either.
There are wounds time just doesn't dull.
Can't go into detail, but I find myself keeping people at a distance without even meaning to.
You're back. I was waiting.
I start worrying when you don't show your face for a while.

low: Café did decent business again today.
Thursdays I check on the bean roasting.
Coffee smells good again today.

lines: Flora keeps begging me to make her a strawberry latte.
How am I supposed to make something that childish.
fallback_lines: Made myself a strawberry latte today, for the first time in a while.
I know. It's the childish latte that little Flora used to love.

mid: People are strange. You swear you'll never love again, and yet you end up falling in love anyway.

lines: That Marin kid talks about his dad every time I see him. Envious, honestly, that kind of bond.
If only my own guy had been as good a person as Roshi...
fallback_lines: Marin and Roshi really were a close father and son.

mid: I don't think there's a single person in town who hasn't stopped by my café.
high: I was married once, you know. Now, though... it's all in the past.
Seeing you again, {player_name}. How are you feeling today?
I've got a lot on my mind. Not sure the choices I've made were the right ones.
Still, I probably made the best choice I could at the time, right?
I'm trying not to regret it.

low: Another week's over. Have a cup of coffee before you go.
Customers pick up a bit on Friday evenings. Guess everyone's wrapping up the week.
Didn't raise coffee prices again this week. Even though bean prices keep going up.
mid: What menu item do you think I should add to the café?

options.label: How about a sweet dessert?
response: Oh, nice. I've been craving something sweet lately too.
I'll look into a recipe. You're taste-testing first, got it?

options.label: Isn't the current menu perfect already?

response.text: Don't people only say that when sales are up?

options.label: How about one more menu item with seasonal berries?
response: The berries have been especially good lately anyway.

mid: Do you like lattes more too?
Now that I think about it, seems like more people prefer lattes.
Poli's a regular at my café too. Coffee helps a lot with the morning shift, I guess.
high: You don't know what kind of person I really am. You might be disappointed if you did.
Kind of silly to bring this up at my age.
Someone being disappointed in me isn't such a big deal anyway.
{player_name}, seeing you a lot lately.

high.text: You like this café too, right?

high: I'll set aside a regular seat for you if you want.
Still debating whether to add that menu item you said you wanted last time.

low: The café's busiest on weekends.
Even two hands aren't enough on Saturdays.
I like that weekend customers take their time.

lines: Woody drops by often. She's an easy customer to have around.
I'd love a daughter like her, honestly.
fallback_lines: I always used to think I'd love having a daughter like Woody.
...No, honestly, I still think that now.
I think of her often. Such a sweet kid.

mid: Sage comes by for tea sometimes. Doesn't say much, though.
Is she going for that mysterious act on purpose?
Didn't you run into Poli on your way here?
He usually stops by around this time.
Hm? There's just something personal I wanted to ask him.
high: Lately I grind the beans on purpose to match when you usually come by.
I'll give you a good cup.

high.text: I've kept your seat reserved, wouldn't let anyone else sit there.
Of course, if it gets busy, no exceptions!

high: Sometimes I feel like you're a friend, kind of.
With this age gap between us. Funny, right?

low: Opened up a bit later, more relaxed, on Sunday.
I start Sunday mornings with a cup of coffee myself.
Guess the café smell's soaked into me even on my day off.
mid: On a day like today, I take a break with a cup of coffee myself.

lines: Usher comes by sometimes with a book and just sits there. It's nice, the quiet.
fallback_lines: Even now, that seat over there reminds me of Usher, coming here to write.

mid: On Sundays I like just staring blankly out the window too.
high: Coffee smell's pretty nice, isn't it?
A lot better than walking around smelling of cows or pigs.
Stay a while.

high.text: Seeing your face makes it feel like the whole day's gone right.

high: Just saying.
Well, it's not bad. Keep coming by.
I was sitting alone in the café after all the customers left today.
And out of nowhere, I remembered something I let slide even though I knew it was wrong toward someone.
I think people just do bad things for their own sake sometimes, don't they.

rain_conversation: Rainy days bring more people to the café. Guess everyone craves coffee.
If you don't have an umbrella, rest at the café for a while.
On days like this you have to roast the beans extra carefully so they don't go damp.
mail_reaction: You sent '{player_mail_content}'. Enjoyed reading it. Feel free to send more like that.
About that mail you sent, '{player_mail_content}'. Honestly, it made me laugh a little. No offense meant.

horror_conversation.text: I still keep {victim_name}'s favorite seat open these days.

horror_conversation: Even when it's busy, I won't give that one away. Not even sure why myself.
I thought of {victim_name} out of nowhere while roasting beans. No real reason.

horror_conversation.text: I just never realized talking about someone who's gone would feel this strange.

greeting.title: Today's Bean Recommendation
lines: The beans I roasted today smell especially good.
I'll brew you a cup with these next time you come by.
Don't get so busy you can't even spare time for coffee.

greeting.title: Just Wondering How You're Doing
lines: You've been scarce lately, so I wrote a few lines out of curiosity.
It's been a while since I had the time to write a letter like this, running the shop and all.
Busy or not, doing well or not, either way is fine.

greeting.title: Let Me Brag About a Customer
lines: A stranger told me today that my café makes the best coffee in town.
Couldn't help feeling a little proud.
You think so too, right?

event_invite.title: Had a Great Meal
lines: Thanks for inviting me over yesterday.
Food someone else makes really does taste different.
I'll pay you back with coffee next time.

event_invite.title: That Berry Dish Was Something Else
lines: Can't stop thinking about that berry dish from yesterday.
Wanted to sneak the recipe out, but held back.
Invite me again.

alibi_reminder.title: Everyone's Shaken Up
lines: Heard it happened right outside your house. Must've been a shock, are you okay?
{player_name}, there's something I want to talk about too — could you stop by the café?

gift_thanks.title: Got Your Gift
lines: You didn't have to get me something like this.
Still, I'll gladly take it. Thanks.

gift_thanks.title: How Do I Pay This Back
lines: I'm the type who needs to return what I'm given to feel at ease.
I'll throw in an extra cup of coffee next time you come by. Let's call it even.

memento_reminder.title: You've Been Scarce Lately
lines: Haven't seen your face around in a while.
I've got something set aside for you, come by the café when you have time.

player_arrival_day_3.title: Heard You're New Here?
lines: Heard you just moved into town.
Stop by the café if you're bored. I'll charge you fair prices.
Welcome, {player_name}.
